name: Reduced Motion
summary: Reduced motion is one CSS token that resolves to 1 or 0, and every animation in this library multiplies by it. Use it to honor `prefers-reduced-motion` and to offer a page toggle beside it. The page can only ever add the restriction, because the reader's system setting has to keep the last word.
demoNote: The toggle in example 2 controls every example on this page, and the readout under it names the three signals behind the answer. Example 5 is one extra CSS rule that beats your operating system, with a button that proves it.

contract.useWhen: One motion token: a page can add the restriction, never override the OS.
keyboard: native: reaches the switch and every button on the page
toggles the checkbox behind the switch
native: activates a focused button, and never toggles the switch — a checkbox ignores it
states: not reducing — the absence of the attribute
failureModes: [data-motion="on"], which beats the media query and leaves the toggle unable to describe the page
matchMedia read for the value, which cannot see the page’s own toggle
the distance gated as well as the duration, so a state change becomes a jump cut
a loop past five seconds with no pause control (SC 2.2.2), whatever the motion setting
